content.title: ABC Yanks Pending Season 22 of 'Bachelorette' Following Allegations of Domestic Abuse - Media Play News
content.text: Taylor Frankie Paul March 19, 2026 ABC TV has pulled the pending season 22 of “The Bachelorette,” starring “The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives” alum Taylor Frankie Paul, after allegations of domestic abuse and a fight with her child’s father surfaced in a 2023 social media video. The new season was set to begin airing on March 22, with episodes streaming the next day on Hulu. “In light of the newly released video just surfaced today, we have made the decision to not move forward with the new season of ‘The Bachelorette’ at this time, and our focus is on supporting the family,” a Disney spokesperson said in a media statement. While show remains a significant part of the ABC brand, its popularity has shifted from TV ratings to streaming on Hulu, where the show reportedly adds upwards of 5 million viewers per episode over the season. Separately, Hulu halted production on the fifth season of “The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives,” also co-starring Paul, after cast members collectively agreed they did not feel comfortable continuing given the current situation. The show has become a massive hit for Hulu, becoming the platform’s most-watched unscripted season premiere in 2024, even outperforming “The Kardashians.” Hulu is the primary driver for reaching the coveted 18-49 age demographic among advertisers. In fact, recent franchise premieres have set records as ABC’s most-watched unscripted episodes ever on Hulu.
